rationale: The rejected allocation system treated ordinary room life as a scarce resource: one paper family, one writing family, one chair or shelf family across ten scenes. It therefore rationed the very objects and relationships present in the photographs and pushed later candidates toward globes, prisms, clocks, finish tiles and isolated ornaments. Remove cross-scene group reservations entirely, not merely their error messages. Also replace same-scene group exclusivity with object-level accounting: separately approved books, notebooks and sheets may coexist, as may distinct cushions and throws or a carrier and its contents. Reject duplicate IDs and double-counting of the same physical object, not legitimate shared taxonomy. Catalogue approval, exact mentions, environment restrictions and carrier relationships remain mandatory. Preserve scene diversity through different room structures, subsettings, useful material arrangements and organization, including within the strongest source-supported candidates. Retain the existing semantic phrase checks except the two named safety-treatment families. Repeated safety language is not a diversity failure; repeated room recipes still are. Engineering must update prompt, repair text, camera guidance, catalogue names/notes, lexicon ownership and both duplicate-group validators together. Do not leave hidden one-form-per-bank wording or a repair loop that reintroduces scarcity.
